analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/). The modified EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift updates pagedPoolLocksStepWithSchedulerConfig (head lines ~713-729) and adds widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry (lines ~731-756). Together these assert that Gemma 4's wide plain prefill chunk replaces the solo-prefill stripe, and that paged pool maxPrefillChunk stays at defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens (lockstep with max(chunk, stripe)). That lockstep is a crash-safety precondition: PagedSequenceKV aborts the process if a windowed update exceeds maxPrefillChunk. These tests strengthen that guard rather than weakening it. EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift is a new test file (added, 383 lines). Only its metadata and patch excerpt were supplied, with no numbered head text, so I could not read its body. The production geometry change it covers, in EngineV2Factory and the scheduler config, is outside the supplied evidence and was not examined.

The test code uses no real secrets and makes no network calls. It does not change encryption, attestation, authorization or coordinator-provider protocol behavior. The existing hermetic test environment is unchanged: guard path /dev/null and native KV quantization. Threat T-041 and its prefix-cache/SSD paths are exercised only through existing tests; the head text shows no change to the cache-policy semantics (TTL, HMAC lookup tags, scope) from this PR. Nothing here weakens the T-041 mitigations.

Remaining integration question: the production code change that sets the wide plain chunk for Gemma 4 and the pool-sizing logic is not in this batch. It should be reviewed in its own source units to confirm the pool-chunk lockstep and the memory-budget (DoS, T-029) behavior hold for bidirectional media. No finding is raised from these test files.
